question: What a unit may fall back into, and two corrections to land-battle.json found while the rewrite's land combat was built from it.

addresses.name: CUnit::CanRetreatToProvince
addresses.comment: CUnit slot 19, what CUnit::FindRetreatProvince asks of each land province next to the unit. False unless the target is the province the unit is in or one it has an edge to. Then true where **no enemy land strength stands in the target** (EnemyLandStrengthIn under 1) and either the target's controller is no enemy of the unit's owner or the unit's average organisation (slot 20) is at least 1000 - so a unit that still has an organisation of one may fall back onto an enemy's undefended ground. The name is the maintainer's, from his own Ghidra project. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end, `ret 4` twice: the walk of the unit's province's edges, the call of CCountry::IsEnemy at 0x5C5CFC, the compare with the dword at 0x170D7EC (1000) at 0x5C5D17, the call of EnemyLandStrengthIn at 0x5C5D30.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::CountDirections
addresses.comment: CLandCombatant slot 18: how many distinct provinces this side's units come from. **A unit's province is taken the other way about from CCombat::GetCombatWidth**: the one it is in where that is the battle's own, and otherwise its previous one (+0x134) where it has one - `cmp eax, [combat+0x18]; je` keeps the current province for a unit IN the battle's. The count the stacking and envelopment penalties use. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The listing at 0x56BBDA..0x56BBEB: [unit+0x130] compared with [combat+0x18], `je` past the load of [unit+0x134].
addresses.revises: The comment gave the width's rule for a unit's province; the test is the opposite one.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::PickReinforcement
addresses.comment: **Which reserve comes up.** Tallies the width in use by province of origin over all of the side's units - a unit's province being the one it is in where that is the battle's own and otherwise its previous one where it has one, as in CLandCombatant::CountDirections and not as in CCombat::GetCombatWidth. Then each reserve that can fight, in a battle past its first hour (CCombat +0x1C above 0), makes one draw of the game's generator: `Random() % 100 <= CUnit::ReinforceChance / 10` lets it stand, with CUnit::ReinforceScore - divided by 1000 where its province of origin already uses BASE_COMBAT_WIDTH. The best score wins; null for none. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end with the listing of 0x56B990..0x56BB70, `ret 4`; the origin at 0x56BAD2..0x56BAEA is `cmp eax, [combat+0x18]; je` past the load of [unit+0x134].
addresses.revises: The comment did not say how a unit's province of origin is taken, and the findings file gave the width's rule for it.

addresses.name: ReseedGlobalRandom
addresses.no_signature: not read to its convention; it takes nothing on the stack at its one call site read
addresses.comment: Re-initialises the global generator from the seed at 0x174DA94 through 0xAA2BF0 with g_random_seed in ecx, zeroes the index, and then **runs the generator forward by g_random_draws draws** - so a generator can be put back where a save left it. Two callers: RunHourlyTick at 0x681C79 and 0x6D7BF2. **RunHourlyTick stores the seed first, from the dword at +4 of the hour's tick payload (0x681C6B..0x681C6E), and zeroes g_random_draws**: every hour starts a fresh stream from a figure the tick carries, which is how every machine in a game rolls alike. 0xAA2BF0 itself was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 3, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 1.2.
addresses.evidence: The listing of RunHourlyTick at 0x681C69..0x681C79 and the decompiled loop of this function, which twists and steps the index until a counter reaches g_random_draws.
addresses.revises: The comment did not have where the hourly seed comes from, nor the forward run by the draw count.
